measured.caveat: Measured in a worktree that also held another window's uncommitted work (rust/crates/runtime/src/process_tree.rs and its lib.rs wiring). That file is therefore present in this baseline but not in the branch's committed state, and the run is not reproducible from the commit alone. Re-measure once the branch is the only writer.

floor.reason: Set below the measured Windows baseline on purpose. Coverage is measured on Linux in CI, where #[cfg(unix)] code is compiled and therefore enters the denominator, so the CI number is expected to differ from this one. The floor is a ratchet against a real drop, not a target: raise it to the first measured Linux value minus about one point, and never raise it without a measurement to justify the new value.

not_judged.why: Development-only harness. Its low number is a consequence of being driven by other crates' tests, not of untested product behaviour.
Binary entry point for a test fixture; exercised as a process, so per-line coverage of main is not meaningful.

CLI wiring. The measured 58.40% is mostly argument dispatch and terminal rendering. Do not read the overall number as product assurance while this file dominates the uncovered total (3843 uncovered lines).

limits: Line coverage counts execution, not verification. A line can run without its result being asserted, so this number must never be presented as evidence that a behaviour is correct.
The floor guards against a drop, not against weak tests. Adding a large module with shallow tests can hold the number steady while lowering the quality of the suite.
Only lines that are compiled count. Code behind #[cfg(unix)] or #[cfg(windows)] is invisible to a run on the other platform.
